claim: Dénia's red prawn is caught at ~600m depth between Cape San Antonio and Ibiza, is scarce (one or two boxes per boat per day), best boiled in its own seawater for ~3 minutes with no sauce, and costs roughly €150-170/kg at origin.
quote: no more than one or two boxes of Dénia Red Shrimp to the port each day... boiled in her own seawater and without adding any sauces or garnish... prices range between 150 and 170 euros per kilogram

claim: The Mercat Municipal on Magallanes Street (parallel to Marqués de Campo) opens Monday-Saturday 8:00-15:00, has occupied the site since 1954, and houses a fishmonger nave plus bars and cafés (Bar Magallanes, Viciano Bar, Bonanza Bar) for tapas and wine while shopping.
quote: Monday to Saturday, 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM... Located on Magallanes Street... parallel to Calle Marques de Campo... Five bars and cafés (Bar Magallanes, Viciano Bar, Bonanza Bar)

claim: Dénia was designated a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy in 2015, valuing local produce (red shrimp, fresh fish, cocas), sustainability and traditional knowledge, with a local Bancalet seal certifying proximity origin.
quote: values the quality of its cuisine, but also its commitment to sustainability, innovation and the transmission of gastronomic knowledge... Bancalet... a declaration of love for the product of proximity

claim: Calle Loreto is popularly known as the street of restaurants with a high concentration of tapas and rice offerings; Baix la Mar is a colorful pedestrianized old fishing quarter; Marqués de Campo is a pedestrianized boulevard of busy café terraces.
quote: Loreto Street is popularly known as the street of the restaurants... a very high concentration of local gastronomic offerings, ideal for enjoying tapas and rice dishes... low houses in bright colors and charming squares

claim: Arròs a banda originated with Alicante fishermen who used low-value fish to make an intense stock in which rice was then cooked, the rice traditionally served separately ('a banda') from the fish.
quote: originated with the fishermen of Alicante, who sold off their best fish and kept the leftovers for stock, in which rice was cooked

claim: Dénia rice specialists for arròs a banda and seafood rice include El Pegolí (classic arròs a banda, since 1943), Casa Federico (over twenty rice varieties), Haití (choose your socarrat level), and Restaurante Mena on the Les Rotes cliffs.
quote: El Pegolí has been living history since 1943, and its classic arròs a banda is essential... Haití allows you to choose the level of socarrat... Restaurante Mena is perched on the cliffs

claim: Dénia hosts an annual International Creative Cuisine Competition of the Dénia Red Prawn, which draws chefs from across Spain and reinforces the city's gastronomic profile.
quote: The red prawn once again challenges culinary creativity in Dénia with a new edition of its International Competition
